Subject (in full) Communist Meeting in Western Chapei re: transient "tai-kung"
strike at N.W.K. No.2 Cotton Mill.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa. Forwarded by [Signature]

With reference to the attached translation of extract from
the French Police Intelligence Report of February 20, 1933,
Agent A-4727 reports that the meeting referred in question was
held between 9 and 10.30 a.m. February 18, 1933 in a Chinese
dwelling, No.345 Pan Ka Wan (潘家湾) Road near the Dah Fung (大丰).
Cotton Mill, Western Chapei, and was attended by eleven
communist adherents. Lao Wong (老黄), member of the Shanghai
Western Special District Committee of the local Chinese Communist
Party, who presided over the meeting, announced that the "tai-
Kung" strike which had occurred at No. 2 N.W.K. Cotton Mill on February 15
had been a failure because of the absence of proper leadership
which resulted in the apprehension of two female workers by the
imperialistic Kuomintang. He suggested that henceforth workers
should not remain on the factory but leave the premises or
besiege the offices.
The meeting decided to call on the workers of other
factories to support the struggle and to further communist
propaganda on the Japanese atrocities perpetrated since
February 28, 1932.
In connection with the agitation at the N.W.K. Mills,
I forward herewith, together with summarized translations, copies
of two communist handbills entitled "Letter to Workers of Nos. 1
and 2 N.W.K. Cotton Mills opposing the oppression and dismissal
of workers by the Japanese imperialistic capitalists" and
"Letter to Japanese Factory Workers in the Western District
opposing the dismissal of workers in Nos. 1 and 2 N.W.K.
Cotton Mills by the Japanese Imperialistic Capitalists" purporting
to emanate from the Shanghai Western District Committee of the
Chinese Communist Party which were obtained by the aforementioned

日期：1933年2月22日。

主题（全称）：关于西北纺织株式会社第二棉纺厂临时“怠工”罢工的闸北西部共产党会议。

由督察顾宝华（Kuh Pao-hwa）撰写。经由 [签名] 转呈

参照附上的1933年2月20日法国警察情报报告摘录译文，
特工 A-4727 报告称，所述会议于1933年2月18日上午9时至10时30分在闸北西部大丰（Dah Fung）棉纺厂附近潘家湾路345号的一户华人住宅内举行，共有十一名共产党追随者出席。主持会议的中共上海西区特别区委委员老黄（Lao Wong）宣布，2月15日发生在西北纺织株式会社第二棉纺厂的“怠工”罢工因缺乏适当领导而失败，导致两名女工被帝国主义国民党逮捕。他建议此后工人不应留在工厂内，而应离开工厂或包围办公处。
会议决定号召其他工厂的工人支持此次斗争，并进一步宣传自1932年2月28日以来日本人所犯下的暴行。
关于西北纺织株式会社各厂的煽动活动，现随函附上两份共产党传单的副本及其摘要译文，标题分别为《致西北纺织株式会社第一、二棉纺厂工人书——反对日本帝国主义资本家压迫和解雇工人》和《致西区日本工厂工人书——反对日本帝国主义资本家解雇西北纺织株式会社第一、二棉纺厂工人》，据称出自中国共产党上海西区委员会，系上述

Summarized translation of a communist handbill entitled
"Letter to Workers of Nos. 1 and 2 N.W.K. Cotton Mills
Opposing the Oppression and dismissal of Workers by the
Japanese Imperialistic Capitalists," purporting to emanate
from the Shanghai Western District Committee of the Chinese
Communist Party which was obtained by the Municipal Police
in Western Chapei on February 21, 1933.

Rise and unite, the entire body of workers of Nos.1 and
2 N.W.K. Cotton Mills !

The Japanese imperialists are contemplating
launching a general offensive on Jehol on February 25.
As they will intensify their attack day by day, the whole
area in the North-East will be under their invasion and
massacre.

Labourers, the Japanese capitalists at the instance
of their imperialists, are oppressing you in the worst
manner, dismiss and assault labourers, and cancel bonuses
and other allowances. On the other hand the Kuomintang -
the imperialistic running dog - have done their utmost in
rendering assistance to the Japanese capitalists . They
arrest labourers and suppress strikes.

You should therefore rise and unite and join the
Chinese Communist Youth League in order to overthrow the
imperialistic capitalists and the Kuomintang with a view
to achieving final victory. The following are our slogans :
1. Demand the immediate release of the arrested labourers.
2. Oppose the dismissal of and assault on workers and
reinstate the dismissed workers.
3. Permanent employ be given to casual workers.
4. Resume the issue of rice allowance and other bonuses.

Shanghai Western District Committee
of the Chinese Communist Party.

题为《致西北纺织株式会社第一、二棉纺厂工人书——反对日本帝国主义资本家压迫和解雇工人》的共产党传单摘要译文，据称出自中国共产党上海西区委员会，系工部局警务处于1933年2月21日在闸北西部查获。

西北纺织株式会社第一、二棉纺厂全体工人，起来团结起来！

日本帝国主义者正策划于2月25日对热河发动全面进攻。
随着他们日复一日地加强攻击，整个东北地区将遭受他们的入侵和屠杀。

劳工们，日本资本家在其帝国主义者的指使下，以最恶劣的方式压迫你们，解雇并殴打劳工，取消奖金和其他津贴。另一方面，国民党——帝国主义的走狗——竭尽全力协助日本资本家。他们逮捕劳工并镇压罢工。

因此，你们应该起来团结起来，加入中国共产主义青年团，以推翻帝国主义资本家和国民党，从而取得最终胜利。我们的口号如下：
1. 要求立即释放被捕劳工。
2. 反对解雇和殴打工人，恢复被解雇工人的工作。
3. 给予临时工永久雇佣地位。
4. 恢复发放米贴及其他奖金。

中国共产党上海西区委员会。

Summarized translation of a communist handbill entitled
"Letter to Japanese Factory Workers in the Western District
Opposing the Dismissal of workers in Nos. 1 and 2 N.W.K.
Cotton Mills by the Japanese Imperialistic Capitalists",
purporting to emanate from the Shanghai Western District
Committee of the Chinese Communist Party which was obtained
by the Municipal Police in Western Chapei on February 21, 1933.

Rise and unite, Japanese factory workers in the Western District!

While the Japanese imperialists are intensifying
their attack in the North East, the Japanese capitalists in
Shanghai are seriously opposing us and encroaching on our
interests. The workers in Nos. 1 and 2 mills have succeeded
in their anti-Japanese imperialistic and anti-capitalists
struggle. Their bonuses, rice allowance and etc. have
been restored.

You are also workers employed in Japanese factories
and you are equally badly treated. You should therefore
rise and overthrow the imperialistic capitalists and the
Kuomintang who are assisting the imperialists to arrest
labourers. The workers in Nos. 1 and 2 mills have set a
good example. You should join the Chinese Communist Youth
League which is the only way to attain your object. Our slogans
are as follows :-

1. Demand the immediate release of all arrested workers.
2. Oppose the dismissal of workers.
3. Reinstate dismissed workers.
4. Action to be taken against foremen who assault workers.
5. Resume issue of bonuses, rice allowance and give permanent
employ to casual workers.

Shanghai Western District Committee
of the Chinese Communist Party.

题为《致西区日本工厂工人书——反对日本帝国主义资本家解雇西北纺织株式会社第一、二棉纺厂工人》的共产党传单摘要译文，据称出自中国共产党上海西区委员会，系工部局警务处于1933年2月21日在闸北西部查获。

西区日本工厂工人们，起来团结起来！

当日本帝国主义者加强在东北的攻击时，上海的日本资本家正在严重反对我们并侵犯我们的利益。第一、二厂的工人在其反日本帝国主义和反资本家的斗争中取得了成功。他们的奖金、米贴等已得到恢复。

你们也是受雇于日本工厂的工人，同样受到恶劣待遇。因此，你们应该起来推翻帝国主义资本家以及协助帝国主义者逮捕劳工的国民党。第一、二厂的工人树立了良好的榜样。你们应该加入中国共产主义青年团，这是实现你们目标的唯一途径。我们的口号如下：

1. 要求立即释放所有被捕工人。
2. 反对解雇工人。
3. 恢复被解雇工人的工作。
4. 对殴打工人的工头采取行动。
5. 恢复发放奖金、米贴，并给予临时工永久雇佣地位。

中国共产党上海西区委员会。

Labour (4)

N.W.K. No. 2 Mill - Transient strike

At 6.00 p.m. February 17 while the night shift
workers in the weaving Room of the N.W.K. No. 2 Mill,
60 Robison Road, O.O.L. were taking over the Room from
the day shift, some of the latter carried out agitation
by instigating the night workers to declare a strike to
demand better conditions. Work ceased at 6.10 p.m.
when the 130 workers of the Room went on strike. They
resumed unconditionally however at 6.35 p.m. the same
evening.

Extract from Intelligence Report 17.2.33.

N.W.K. No.2 Mill - transient stoppage of work

At 12 noon February 16, the Chinese Police from
the 6th District Police Station called at the above
mentioned Mill, 60 Robinson Road, O.O.L. and took into
custody the two female workers who were responsible
for the 'tai-kung' strike of the concern on February
15 with the intention of questioning them on the matter.
As a consequence, the 300 workers in the Mill immediately
declared a 'tai-kung' strike in support of their colleagues,
but resumed half an hour later on the advice of an overseer
of the concern.

pages.en:
Extract from the Daily Report of Inspector in charge of
Pootoo Road Station dated 16/2/33

At 9.45 p.m. February 15, Inspector Shibuye
reported at the Station that a strike had occurred at
No.2 N.W.K. Mill, 62 Robison Road, O.O.L. Enquiries
ascertained that on the 14-2-33, three females had been
fighting and generally creating a disturbance in the
Weaving Room. These females were warned and later
escorted away from the Mill by a Sikh Watchman. Having
returned to work on night shift, the 15th inst., they
complained of having lost face and managed to excite
sympathy from the more unruly females. At 7.30 p.m.
February 15, the work ceased in the Weaving Room and
immediately afterwards in the Spinning Room. Approximately
625 hands were concerned. A Japanese Foreman Yomomato
entering the Spinning Room saw a male worker leading a
number of females and strike one of machines with a wooden
bar. The foreman remonstrated with him, when he then
struck the Japanese about the face and body. This man
was later arrested and charged with assault by the No.6
Division, S.P.S. Bureau. A certain number of machines
were temporarily put out of commission. About 20 of the
workers have been dismissed. The matter appears to have
been amicably settled at 5 a.m. and everything was quite.
In case of further trouble the Chapel Police are keeping
watch and the Pootoo Road Police on Robison Road outside
the premises. The arrested male was brought to the
Station at 12.15 a.m. after the incident had been reported
to J.D.C. 83. At 2 a.m. Sub-Inspector Kae of the Sub-
Station Robison Road came to the Station and requested
that the accused be handed over to him to be dealt with,
as the accused was a resident of Chapel and that the crime
had been committed in Chinese territory. It was
explained to him that the man was being charged from this
Station as an understanding between the parties concerned
allowed the Settlement Police in the Mill. By further
arrangements made at the Mill, S.I. Kae stated that he
would be satisfied to take the man to the 6th Division
where his Superior could make immediate enquiries regarding
the cause of the Strike and the Assault and guaranteed the
man would be returned in time to be taken to the S.S.M. Court
at 7 a.m. 16/2/33. With a view to fostering friendly
relations, this was allowed, but on arrival at the No.6
Station the Settlement Police were informed that the man
would be detained by the Chapel Police and charged by them,
as the offence was committed in Chapel and therefore beyond
the jurisdiction of the S.M. Police. Colonel Tan Ke Shao,
Officer in charge No.6 Division was interviewed, but he
refused to return the prisoner, as he maintained the crime
did not concern the Settlement authorities. The D.O. "B"
Division was informed of the accused being detained by the
6th Division Station, and gave instructions that as the
accused was at present in the custody of the Chapel Police
and as they refused to return him, the matter would be
better left for enquiry by the respective headquarters.
For full details see F.I.R. 68/33.
pages.zh:
普陀路巡捕房主管督察1933年2月16日日报告摘录

1933年2月15日晚上9时45分，Shibuye 督察向巡捕房报告称，位于罗宾森路62号（外侨居留地界限以外）的西北纺织株式会社第二厂发生罢工。经查询得知，1933年2月14日，三名女性在织布室打架并一般性地制造骚乱。这些女性受到警告，随后由一名锡克教看守带离工厂。2月15日夜班复工后，她们抱怨丢了面子，并设法激起那些较不守规矩的女性的同情。2月15日晚上7时30分，织布室停止工作，紧接着纺纱室也停止工作。涉及约625名工人。一名日本工头 Yomomato 进入纺纱室，看到一名男工带领数名女性，并用木棒击打一台机器。工头与他理论，随后该男子击打了这名日本人的面部和身体。此人随后被第六分区、工部局警务处逮捕并被指控袭击罪。部分机器暂时停用。约20名工人被解雇。此事似乎在凌晨5时和平解决，一切恢复平静。以防 further trouble，闸北警察在监视，普陀路警察在罗宾森路厂外警戒。事发后向 J.D.C. 83 报告，被捕男子于凌晨12时15分被带到巡捕房。凌晨2时，罗宾森路分巡捕房的副督察 Kae 来到巡捕房，要求将被告移交给他处理，因为被告是闸北居民，且犯罪发生在中国地界。向他解释说，此人由本巡捕房起诉，因为有关各方达成的谅解允许租界警察在工厂内执法。通过在工厂做出的进一步安排，副督察 Kae 表示，他愿意将此人带到第六分区，由其上级立即调查罢工和袭击的原因，并保证此人会被及时送回，以便在1933年2月16日上午7时送往上海特区法院。为了促进友好关系，此要求被允许，但当到达第六巡捕房时，租界警察被告知此人将被闸北警察拘留并由他们起诉，因为罪行发生在闸北，因此超出上海公共租界警务处的管辖范围。第六分区主管谭凯少（Tan Ke Shao，音译）上校接受了面谈，但他拒绝归还囚犯，因为他坚持认为该犯罪与租界当局无关。“B”分区值班警官获悉被告被第六分区巡捕房拘留，并指示鉴于被告目前由闸北警察羁押且他们拒绝归还，此事最好留给各自总部进行调查。详细情况见 F.I.R. 68/33。

N.W.K. No.2 Mill - transient 'tai-kung' strike
As a protest against the dismissal of two of their
colleagues who were alleged to have quarrelled with an
Indian watchman of the concern, the 300 night shift female
workers of the above mentioned 1, 60 Robinson Road,
O.O.L. declared a tai-kung stri.. at 8 p.m. February 15.
They however, resumed at 1 a.m. February 16 when the manage-
ment promised to reinstate the two dismissed workers.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
Pootoo Road....Station,
REPORT
Date 16th. February 33.

Subject (in full) Further unrest amongst the workers of No.2. N.W.K.Mill at
62 Robison Road.
Made by D.J. Guess. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
I have to report that at 6.30.p.m. this inst. Insp.Shibou
received information from No.2 N.W.K. Mill to the effect that
the female workers had called a strike. D.J. Guess immediately
immediately proceeded to the mill and met J.D.C.106 and there
ascertained that the strike finished at 6.35.p.m.
Enquiries were made by J.D.C.s. 106 and 83 and the
undersigned and it was learned that at 6.00.p.m. the night shift
workers attached to the weaving room entered and were about to
take over from the day shift when some of the day shift workers
started to cause unrest by suggesting that they strike for better
condition of work generally. Work ceased at 6.10.p.m. but was
confined to the weaving room, no other departments being concerned.
The mill management immediately made enquiries but no
direct demands were made to the management. The strike suggestion
was not well received by the night shift and work was unconditionally
resumed at 6.35.p.m.
I have to report that at the time of report the Chapei
Police Sub-station in close vicinity to the mill immediately
posted men in the mill and Sub.Insp.Koo commenced his enquiries.
After the workers had resumed work at 6.35.p.m. about 12 Chapei
Uniformed Policemen from the sub-station were left in the mill.
The mill authorities appear to be on very friendly terms with the
local Chapei station.
There were no disturbances outside the mill but patrols
will be detailed to keep observation outside the mill during the
early hours of 18.2.1933.

[Signature]
D.S.263.

（左侧批注：1. R. 19.2.33. h3）

Sen.Det. I/c. [Signature] 16/2/33

普陀路（Pootoo Road）....分局，
报告
日期：1933年2月16日。

主题（全称）：关于罗宾森路（Robison Road）62号西北纺织厂（N.W.K. Mill）第二厂工人中进一步的不安情况。
呈报人：D.J. Guess。转呈人：[签名]

先生，
谨此报告，今日下午6时30分，Shibou巡官接到来自西北纺织厂第二厂的消息，称女工已发起罢工。D.J. Guess随即立即前往该厂，会见了警员编号106（J.D.C.106），并在那里查明罢工已于下午6时35分结束。

经警员编号106和83以及本报告人查询，获悉下午6时，附属于织布车间的夜班工人进入厂区，准备接替白班，此时部分白班工人开始煽动不安，建议为普遍改善工作条件而罢工。下午6时10分工作停止，但仅限于织布车间，其他部门未受影响。

厂方管理层立即进行了查询，但工人方面并未向管理层提出直接要求。夜班工人对罢工提议反应冷淡，工作于下午6时35分无条件恢复。

谨此报告，在撰写本报告时，紧邻该厂的闸北警察分所立即在该厂部署了人员，副巡官顾（Koo）开始了他的调查。在工人于下午6时35分复工后，约有12名来自该分所的闸北制服警察留守厂内。厂方当局似乎与当地闸北分局关系非常友好。

厂外未发生骚乱，但将指派巡逻人员在1933年2月18日凌晨时段在厂外保持监视。

[签名]
D.S.263.

（左侧批注：1. R. 1933年2月19日. h3）

高级侦探主管 [签名] 1933年2月16日
D.D. O'Neil 代理处长
